memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Then they and their children are to be released, and they will go back to
their own clans and to the property of their ancestors. Because the
Israelites are my servants, whom I brought out of Egypt, they must not be
sold as slaves'" - Lev 25:41-42 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At the Jubilee, the indentured person and their children went free, back to
their family and their ancestral land. And God gives the reason: the
Israelites are my servants. They already belonged to God. They could not be
permanently owned by another, because they were His.

That is the deepest ground for their freedom. It was not merely humanitarian
policy. It was ownership. They belonged to God, so no one else could hold
them forever.

Dear reader, this speaks powerfully to the believer. Paul writes, you were
bought at a price; do not become slaves of human beings (1 Cor 7:23). You
belong to God. That belonging is the root of a freedom no one can override.

Whatever tries to master you — an addiction, another person's control, the
approval of the crowd, the tyranny of fear — none of these can permanently
own you, because you already belong to Someone else. Jesus said, if the Son
sets you free, you will be free indeed (John 8:36).

Notice that the children went free too. Freedom in God's design was not just
for the individual but reached into the next generation. What God frees, He
frees thoroughly.

You are God's servant, brought out of a greater Egypt by a greater Exodus.
Live as one who belongs to Him alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has been trying to master me that I need to be freed from?
2. Do I live as one who belongs wholly to God?
3. How might my freedom in Christ bless the next generation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I belong to You, bought by the blood of Jesus. Free me from
everything that tries to master me, and let me live as Your servant alone.
Amen.
